### This is a beta release

This build is for testing only. It is published as a pre-release, so it is not offered to
existing installations through the in-app updater — install it by hand from the assets below.

### What this build is for: the Windows upgrade path

It is the last thing standing between here and the stable release. The app was renamed to
DisplayMuxAuto, and NSIS recognises an earlier version **by product name** — so a renamed app
finds nothing to replace and installs beside the old copy instead of over it. That is not merely
a spare folder: autostart is registered by product name too, so the old copy would go on starting
at login, and two copies cannot share one agent port or one mDNS name. The symptom looks like
pairing being broken.

beta.8 added a pre-install cleanup step. It compiles on CI, but it has **never run on a real
Windows machine**.

**Install this build over an older one** (any version still called DisplayMux) and confirm three
things:

1. Apps & Features lists only DisplayMuxAuto
2. The old install folder is gone
3. **After a reboot only one copy is running** — the most important one; if the autostart entry
   survives, the two copies fight each other

### Fixes

- **The global host switcher had never worked on macOS.** The default shortcut was
  `Command+Option+Space`, which macOS binds to its Finder search window. Registration reports
  success and the key never arrives — no error, no log, a settings page that looks correct. The
  default is now `Command/Ctrl+Shift+Space`; combinations the system reserves are refused when a
  shortcut is recorded, with the reason; and a saved one is replaced at startup and written back.
- **One successful switch left the switcher unusable for good**, reopening included. The window
  is hidden rather than closed, and the flag marking a switch in progress was cleared only on
  failure — while that flag gates every row, every key press, and the refresh that runs when the
  window is shown again, so the path back was closed too.
- **The switcher no longer offers the host a display is already showing.** It had no way to know
  which one that was, so it listed it like any other; pressing it reached the backend, which
  correctly answered that the display was already on that input, and the window sat on the
  message. That row is now labelled, not selectable, and skipped by the arrow keys, as on the
  dashboard.
- **A rejected setting is no longer reported as a display failure.** A shortcut the system
  reserves, a password that is too short, two hosts on one port — all arrived prefixed "unable to
  complete the display operation", pointing at hardware that was fine. Eleven messages changed.
- The sidebar no longer squashes the app icon out of shape (the name grew by four letters and the
  icon was the only thing in that row that could give).
- The reset warning reads as a warning rather than as a disabled field.

### Known limitations

- Undoing a merge leaves the inputs and notes that merging folded into the display the other
  identity joined.
- Ports, merges and host names only sync between hosts running this version.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed but not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may
  require manual approval.

### What to test

- **Windows: install this build over an older one** and confirm the three things above.
- macOS: press `Command+Shift+Space`, switch once, summon it again, and confirm it still responds.
